questions.prompt: When control flows OUTWARD across a boundary, which way does the source-code dependency point, and why?

options.text: Outward too, because control and dependencies always match
Inward, because the inner component calls through an interface it owns that the outer component implements
Inward, but only in compiled languages

questions.explanation: Calling 'against the flow' is handled by dependency inversion: the inner side calls through an owned interface, so control flows out while the source dependency points in.

options.text: The interface a driver uses to invoke a use case
An interface the use case owns and calls to send results outward, implemented by an outer component
The entity that holds the result

questions.explanation: An output port is owned by the use case and called to report results; a presenter (outer) implements it. The interface a driver invokes is the input port.

questions.prompt: The plain data structures created specifically to carry a use case's inputs and outputs across a boundary are the request and ______ models.
questions.explanation: Request and response models are purpose-built structures that cross the boundary instead of entities or ORM objects.

questions.prompt: What should cross an architectural boundary? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Cross boundaries with plain, dedicated request/response models. Passing entities or ORM rows couples the two sides and can violate the Dependency Rule.

questions.prompt: Order a full boundary crossing for one feature.

items.text: Calls the output port with a response model

questions.explanation: Control marches from the controller through the input port to the interactor, then out through the output port to the presenter — while dependencies point inward.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its role.

pairs.right: Interface a use case exposes to be driven
Interface a use case calls to report results
Plain structure carrying inputs across the boundary
A crossing where control goes outward

questions.explanation: Input/output ports and request/response models are the machinery that lets control cross a boundary while dependencies stay inward.
